front.title: Attested Conduct for Anonymous Web Data Collection: Use Cases, Requirements, and a Tiered Model

abstract.t: Anonymous Bot Authentication lets a web site learn that an automated client holds a credential from an Anchor whose policies it accepts, without learning which client it is. This document describes web data collection use cases that need that property, and what they require of the evidence an Anchor evaluates, of what a site can verify about conduct it cannot attribute, and of what a buyer of collected data needs to see. It proposes a tiered model. Collectors register signed statements of their own conduct in a SCITT Transparency Service; the site, its security intermediary, or a network intermediary may corroborate them; and an Anchor acting as a certifying body may appraise them. Coarse, unlinkable attributes about the data's eventual recipient let a site restrict use by category of recipient without learning who the recipient is.
